# Behavioral Specification: OTP Life Cycle Interface (LCI)

## 1. Overview

The Life Cycle Interface (LCI) is the hardware agent responsible for programming the OTP life-cycle partition on behalf of the life-cycle controller. It receives a transition request containing a newly encoded life-cycle state and transition count, writes that payload into the OTP life-cycle partition, and reports whether the programming operation succeeded or failed.

The module has the following general responsibilities:

- Program the life-cycle partition only.
- Never read from the OTP.
- Treat the supplied life-cycle payload as opaque data.
- Write the payload without modification.
- Report completion to the requester.
- Report persistent error status to OTP error handling logic.
- Lock down further programming after a terminal error or escalation event.

## 2. Reset and Enable Behavior

After reset, the module shall be in an inactive state. While inactive:

- No OTP write commands shall be issued.
- No transition request shall be accepted.
- No completion response shall be generated.
- The persistent error status shall be “no error”.
- The programming-idle indicator shall be deasserted.

The module shall remain inactive until the enable indication is asserted. Once enabled, the module shall enter an idle state and wait for a transition request.

In the idle state:

- The programming-idle indicator shall be asserted.
- A transition request may be accepted.
- No OTP activity shall occur until a request is received.

If the escalation indication is active, it shall override the enable behavior and place the module into the terminal error state even if the module has not yet been enabled.

## 3. Transition Request Handling

A transition request consists of a request qualifier and an associated payload. The payload contains the encoded life-cycle state and transition count to be programmed into OTP. The module shall treat this payload as opaque data and shall not parse, decode, verify, or modify its contents.

The module shall accept a transition request only when all of the following conditions are true:

- The module is enabled.
- The module is idle.
- The module is not in the terminal error state.

When a transition request is accepted, the module shall begin a programming sequence. The request and payload must remain stable until the completion response is returned.

The module shall not accept another transition request while a programming sequence is in progress.

The module shall not provide a completion response for a request that is ignored while the module is inactive or in the terminal error state.

## 4. OTP Programming Sequence

The module shall program the entire life-cycle payload into the OTP life-cycle partition. The programming sequence shall write one native OTP word at a time, in address order, starting at the base address of the life-cycle partition.

The number of native OTP words to be written shall be equal to the configured life-cycle partition size divided by the native OTP word width.

For each word in the sequence:

- The module shall issue a write command to the OTP.
- The transfer size shall indicate exactly one native OTP word.
- The write address shall be the life-cycle partition base address plus the current word index.
- The write data shall be the corresponding native word from the supplied payload.
- The selected word shall be placed in the low-order bits of the OTP write data bus.
- The write data bus shall be zero when no write command is being requested.

The module shall hold the OTP write request until the OTP interface accepts the command. After acceptance, the module shall wait for the OTP response before issuing the next write command.

The module shall not issue a subsequent write command until the response for the previous write command has been received.

The module shall issue write commands only. It shall not issue read commands. Any read data returned as part of an OTP response shall be ignored.

The module shall continue the sequence through all words, even if an earlier word in the sequence reported an error, unless escalation has become active.

## 5. Completion Response

The module shall generate exactly one completion response at the end of a programming sequence, after all words have been written or attempted.

If no error was observed during the programming sequence, the module shall:

- Assert the success completion response.
- Return to the idle state.
- Keep the persistent error status at “no error”.

If an error was observed during the programming sequence, the module shall:

- Assert the failure completion response.
- Enter the terminal error state.
- Keep the persistent error status set to the recorded error code.

The completion response shall be generated only after the final OTP word response has been processed. No completion response shall be generated for a request that was not accepted.

## 6. Error Handling

The OTP interface may return an error code in response to a write command. Any non-zero error code shall be treated as a programming error.

When an OTP error is received, the module shall:

- Record the error code.
- Continue attempting to program all remaining words in the sequence, unless escalation is active.
- Use the recorded error when determining the final completion response.

If multiple OTP errors occur during one programming sequence, the persistent error status shall reflect the most recent non-zero error code returned by the OTP.

If a write operation attempts to clear a bit that has already been programmed, the OTP shall report a write-blank error. The module shall treat this error in the same manner as any other OTP programming error.

The persistent error status shall be:

- “No error” after reset.
- Updated when an OTP error is recorded.
- Updated to the illegal-control-state error code if an illegal internal control state is detected.
- Held stable in the terminal error state.
- Cleared only by reset.

The module shall not interpret error codes beyond distinguishing zero from non-zero. The detected error code shall be reported through the persistent error status and shall influence the final completion response.

## 7. Escalation Handling

The escalation indication is active-level. Any value other than the defined OFF value shall be treated as active.

Escalation shall take precedence over all normal module behavior.

When escalation is active, the module shall:

- Immediately enter the terminal error state.
- Stop issuing any further OTP write commands.
- Abandon any programming sequence in progress.
- Not wait for the response of an outstanding OTP command.
- Not accept any further transition requests.
- Not generate new completion responses after the cycle in which escalation is recognized.

If no error code has already been recorded, the persistent error status shall be set to the illegal-control-state error code. If an error code has already been recorded, that existing error code shall be retained.

Escalation shall be effective in all operating states, including the inactive state, idle state, and during an ongoing programming sequence.

## 8. Terminal Error State

The module shall enter the terminal error state under any of the following conditions:

- An OTP programming error was recorded during a programming sequence.
- Escalation is asserted.
- An illegal internal control state is detected.

In the terminal error state, the module shall:

- Not issue any OTP commands.
- Not accept any transition requests.
- Not generate completion responses for subsequent requests.
- Continue to report the persistent error status.
- Indicate that no programming is in progress.

The programming-idle indicator shall be asserted in the terminal error state. This indicates only that no OTP programming operation is active; it does not indicate that the module is available to accept new requests.

The terminal error state shall persist until reset.

## 9. Programming-Idle Indication

The programming-idle indicator shall reflect whether the module is currently performing an OTP programming operation.

The indicator shall be:

- Deasserted while the module is in the inactive state after reset.
- Asserted when the module is enabled and idle.
- Deasserted while a programming sequence is in progress.
- Asserted in the terminal error state.

The programming-idle indication is not a request-acceptance indication. It only reports whether an OTP programming operation is active.

## 10. Data Transparency

The module shall not change the value of the life-cycle payload.

The module shall not:

- Decode the life-cycle state.
- Decode the transition count.
- Compare the new payload against the current OTP contents.
- Perform a blank check.
- Verify whether the requested transition is legal.
- Compute a digest over the payload.

The OTP storage itself is responsible for rejecting writes that would clear already programmed bits. The module shall report any such rejection as an OTP programming error and follow the error handling behavior described above.

The module shall not provide any readback path for the life-cycle partition. Its only interaction with OTP is the write sequence used to perform a life-cycle transition.
